observable_outcome: A Requirement captured through the real surface can be driven to the state in which a person is asked a question, because one new caller-initiated application command issues the transition that leaves the captured status. Measured at cc17473 it cannot be: domain.RequirementStartFraming appears in exactly two non-test lines, both inside internal/domain/model.go, and in zero non-test lines anywhere else, so the set of Requirement statuses reachable through every application command is the single element {captured} -- which makes the needs-input command V2-065 shipped, and with it cap-human-input-request's declared success condition, not merely unexercised but unobservable. The repair is one command, Service.StartFraming (owner or scheduler caller, idempotent by request_id, gated by domain.Permit with kind claim, staging no outbox item), one route, POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:start-framing, declared in the openapi document, and nothing else: internal/domain is not edited because the transition, its guard and its status already exist; no read model changes because the detail route already reports the status; no owner-console control and no documentation prose. The reachable status set becomes exactly {captured, framing, needs-input, ready} and the six other unissued Requirement commands stay unissued. What fixes the outcome is an executed proof against the real control-plane binary and the real Firestore emulator that a Requirement leaves captured, plus a full-chain proof over the composed HTTP handler that capture -> start-framing -> request-input -> detail-shows-the-question -> answer-input resumes the SAME Requirement, plus the seven-mode control table asserted for the new command. The capability is demonstrable after this task and is NOT claimed exercised: the M5 re-dogfood is the coordinator-owned gate that issues that verdict.

A4. The command. Add Service.StartFraming to a NEW file internal/application/framing.go. internal/application/service.go, human_input.go, ports.go and readmodels.go are prohibited: no existing application file is edited. Shape, following Capture (service.go:743) for the request discipline and RequestHumanInput (human_input.go:460) for the transition: (a) callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner, RoleScheduler) -- exactly Capture's pair; a runner caller is refused; (b) requireRequest(req.RequestID) and requestFingerprint("start-framing", req); (c) s.mutate(ctx, "start-framing:"+req.RequestID, ...) with u.Idempotency(ctx, req.RequestID, "start-framing"), refusing a same-key different-fingerprint request with ErrIdempotencyConflict and replaying the prior response with restoreResponse; (d) read the Requirement, return ErrNotFound if absent; (e) resolve the ControlTarget from u.RequirementRepositoryLink inside the same transaction, empty RepositoryID when unlinked, following Plan's link resolution; (f) evaluate domain.Permit with Kind domain.PermitClaim, with the revision derived from domain.EffectiveControl inside the transaction exactly as Capture derives it -- StartFramingRequest carries NO control_revision, NO repository_id and NO timestamp field; (g) domain.DecideRequirement with domain.RequirementCommand{Kind: domain.RequirementStartFraming, Actor: actor, At: the transaction authority time from the same accessor Service.record uses, ExpectedVersion: req.ExpectedVersion}; (h) u.SaveRequirement(ctx, next, r.Version); (i) s.record with operation "start-framing", aggregate type "requirement", event type "requirement.framing-started", and a nil outbox argument. StartFramingRequest is {RequestID, RequirementID string; ExpectedVersion domain.Version}; StartFramingResponse is {RequirementID string; Status domain.RequirementStatus; Version domain.Version}. Do NOT pass anything to domain.EffectFromPermit. Assert in a test that no outbox item is staged.

Add a table test over all seven control modes asserting the new command's outcome for each: allow ALLOWED, pause-intake ALLOWED, pause-claim DENIED, graceful-stop DENIED, immediate-stop DENIED, emergency-stop DENIED, cancel DENIED. Model it on the existing internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go idiom and record the argv and each cell's measured verdict in the evidence. Assert that every DENIED cell leaves the Requirement status AND version AND the absence of any event byte-unchanged. Two boundaries must be asserted explicitly because they are the reason the kind is claim and not intake: pause-intake ALLOWS framing an already-captured Requirement (finishing what you have) while the same control revision still DENIES a fresh Capture, in the same test run; and emergency-stop DENIES framing, which is the property a permit-free command would not have. Do not edit internal/domain. The transition, its guard and its status all already exist: domain.RequirementStartFraming is admitted from RequirementCaptured and sets RequirementFraming, and the whole task is that the application layer issues a command the domain has always accepted. Add no RequirementCommandKind, no RequirementStatus, no PermitKind and no lease transition, and change no allowed() list. If the repair appears to need a domain edit, the design was departed from: stop and escalate.

Do not add a second way to leave the captured status. Exactly ONE command issues domain.RequirementStartFraming when this task lands, and the count is asserted. Do not advance the Requirement inside Service.Capture, do not add a flag to CaptureRequest that advances it, and do not add a reconciler or scheduler sweep that walks captured Requirements: each of those lets a Requirement leave captured without a caller asking for that transition, which is non_goals item 2.

Do not make the command scheduler-only. Measured at cc17473: no non-test code path anywhere constructs an application.Caller with RoleScheduler -- every real caller is owner or runner, from internal/api/auth.go -- so a scheduler-only command would be unreachable over both the production IAP boundary and the preview-local boundary, which is this task's own defect reproduced one level up. The route must remain owner-callable. If you find a transport that does produce a scheduler caller, escalate the finding rather than narrowing the route.

Do not remove the Permit to make a test pass, and do not copy Plan's and Prepare's permit-free shape. The kind is domain.PermitClaim, evaluated with domain.Permit alone; nothing is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit, because no durable effect is staged and EffectFromPermit requires the effective mode to be exactly allow, which would wrongly deny framing under pause-intake. The seven-mode table in A5 is the design: if any cell measures differently, stop and escalate.

Do not accept a control revision, a repository id or a timestamp from the caller. The revision comes from domain.EffectiveControl inside the transaction as Capture derives it, the repository comes from the Requirement's own link as Plan resolves it, and the instant comes from the transaction authority accessor Service.record uses. A caller-supplied value for any of the three is refused, not honoured.
